lines.name: H1 Monochrome: is intentional rasterisation acceptable, or is a structure-preserving implementation required?
lines.detail: recommendation: Keep rasterisation (candidate A) for the M5 MVP only as an explicit INTENTIONAL_FLATTENING operation whose PLAN names every loss and requires confirmation; take candidate C (structure-preserving, fail-closed) forward as a separate spike measured on real drawings before it is offered.

lines.name: H2 Optimize: what does 「最適化」 promise as a product contract (O1 flatten / O2 lossless / O3 preservation levels), and may the name stay?
lines.detail: recommendation: Do not keep O1 under the name 「最適化」: measured, it removes all text/structure and makes vector drawings 12-463x larger. Either rename O1 to an explicit flattening operation (e.g. 画像化) or make 「最適化」 mean O2/O3 (structure kept, images recompressed, never larger).

lines.name: H3 Margin: which source structure must survive (text, OCR, annotations, links, forms, /Rotate, CropBox, metadata)?
lines.detail: recommendation: All of them. The in-place candidate keeps every measured property and matches the expected picture on every rotation and crop fixture; it refuses annotations it cannot move and content that underflows q/Q.

lines.name: H4 Batch failure: fail whole (B1), explicit partial with a manifest (B2), or independent per-file jobs (B3)?
lines.detail: recommendation: B2 — the successes ship only with a manifest naming every failure and why, in the archive and on screen; today's partial ZIP carries no record of the failure.

lines.name: H5 Searchable text / OCR: may an intentionally flattening operation remove it, and on what confirmation?
lines.detail: recommendation: Only with an explicit, per-run confirmation that names the loss; never as a default and never silently.

lines.name: H6 Annotations and forms: preserve, refuse, or explicitly flatten — per operation?
lines.detail: recommendation: Structure-preserving operations preserve (and transform) them or refuse; flattening operations list them among the confirmed losses.

lines.name: H7 Signatures and XFA: exact refusal policy, and does it apply to the hardened lanes too?
lines.detail: recommendation: Reuse the existing read-only assessSource in a common PLAN step for every Processor operation, the hardened lanes included: signed → SIGNATURE_UNSAFE, XFA → XFA_UNSAFE, encrypted → refused. It adds a refusal to the hardened lanes and removes nothing they guarantee.

lines.name: H8 Memory budget for full-page raster operations: default and explicit override policy?
lines.detail: recommendation: A per-page preflight on raster pixels and the measured browser canvas limit, with an M4-style explicit override for memory; its constants to be measured for this pipeline, not copied from M4.

lines.name: H9 Raster resolution: which DPI are offered per operation and sheet, and how is an impossible one refused without a silent downgrade?
lines.detail: recommendation: Offer only what the preflight accepts for the chosen sheets; a request over the canvas limit (A1/A0 at 600 dpi today) is refused before the first page with the numbers, never reduced.

lines.name: H10 Cancellation: atomic output and ownership — does a settings change, file change or navigation supersede a run?
lines.detail: recommendation: Yes: the F1-B/M4 owner token, captured at start and re-read at every file boundary and immediately before the single publish; unmount, a settings change and a file-list change all supersede.

lines.name: H11 Common Processor orchestration: one PLAN/RESULT engine, or per-tool engines?
lines.detail: recommendation: One orchestration (source inspection, raster preflight, ownership, batch policy, publish) with per-operation planners and runners; the hardened lanes enter it unchanged behind the common inspection step.

lines.name: H12 Metadata: which operations may change the Info dictionary and XMP, and must a flattening operation carry them into the new document?
lines.detail: recommendation: No operation changes metadata silently: preserve Info/XMP (load with updateMetadata: false; copy them into rebuilt documents) unless the Human Gate names a change.

lines.name: H13 Layer: what does the overlay cover — the visible page (CropBox ∩ MediaBox) or the MediaBox from (0,0) — and do annotations sit under it or above it?
lines.detail: recommendation: The visible page, in the page's own coordinates (today it misses 61% of the ink when the MediaBox does not start at the origin); annotation layering stated in the UI either way.
